key_insight: In this benchmark, LLMs detected many inserted methodological errors in clinical trial reports, suggesting a potential role in supporting peer review rather than cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted review could help identify flaws in clinical trial evidence, but the abstract does not establish oncology-specific benefits or improved patient outcomes.
method: Tested 15 LLMs, including four open-weight models, on three trial reports containing inserted errors.
Repeated testing on three trials published in 2026 to reduce memorization risk.
Evaluated error detection and flags in control reports without inserted errors.
evidence_signal: Major-error detection ranged from 53%–96% initially and 51%–99% on newer trials, compared with a 27% mean for untrained human reviewers in an earlier experiment.
watch_item: Models also flagged 2%–29% of error types in unmodified control reports, underscoring the need for expert verification of AI-generated critiques.
paper_title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
